title: HarnessCompass: Guiding Automatic Harness Evolution toward Generalizable and Effective Agent Harnesses
author: Luan Zhang, Ruochen Zhou, Dandan Song, Zhengyu Chen, Yuhang Tian, Jun Yang, Huipeng Ma, Chenhao Li, Guangyuan Feng, Xudong Li, Yizhou Jin, Yan Xu (synthesized by Brain Harness)

claims.assertion: Conventional Automatic Harness Evolution (AHE) overfits to search tasks, accumulating task-specific branches and memorized symbols that degrade held-out generalization.

A Global Generalization Gate enforcing Content Invariants (zero task IDs, test names, or private symbols) and Placement Invariants (Capability in middleware/tools vs Guidance in prompt/memory) improves held-out Pass@1 from 51.6% to 58.4% in 2 iterations.
claims.source: Zhang et al. (arXiv:2608.01918v1, 2026), Table 2 (Ablation on HarnessCompass)

claims.assertion: Eliciting first-person Blind pre-verdict reflections combined with post-verdict failure attribution isolates harness friction from model reasoning and environment noise, avoiding hindsight rationalization bias.
claims.source: Zhang et al. (arXiv:2608.01918v1, 2026), Section 3 (Proactive Feedback) & Appendix A

claims.assertion: Partitioning evolution into disjoint Structural and Guidance tracks and reconciling via R3 (Revision, Recombination, Refinement) achieves 61.0% total Pass@1 in 5 iterations on SWE-Bench Verified (outperforming AHE's 55.5% in 20 iterations) while eliminating advisory prompt bloat.
Harnesses evolved with HarnessCompass transfer across foundational models (e.g. from GPT-5.4 to Claude-Sonnet-4.6) without regression, demonstrating domain-general engineering robustness.
